sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
சிந்தையெல்லாம் நிறைந்தாய் நாராயணா
முந்தை வினையும் வந்த வினையும் களைந்தே என்
sections.translit:
sindhaiyellAm niRaindhAy nArAyaNA
mundhai vinaiyum vandha vinaiyum kaLaindhE en
sections.en: Lord Narayana, you removed all of my past and present sins and have pervaded my mind.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
விந்தையே வடிவானாய் விண்ணுலகின் அரசே
எந்தையே நிகரானாய் பரிந்து தயையும் புரிந்து
sections.translit:
vindhaiyE vadivAnAy viNNulagin arasE
endhaiyE nigarAnAy parindhu dhayaiyum purindhu
sections.en: Oh, supreme Lord of the heavens, you are the personification of wonderment. You are like my father, acting with empathy and compassion and helping me each step of the way.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
கந்தை அணிந்தவன் கைபிடி அவலுக்கடிமையானாய்
நிந்தை செய்தவன் மகன் சொல் காக்க இரு உருவானாய்
பந்தை ஒத்த அளவு வெண்ணை திருடவென்றே நீயும்
மந்தை மேய்ப்பவன் போல் வந்தாய் உருகியே கண்ணீர் பெருகி நின்ற என்
sections.translit:
kandhai aNindhavan kaippidip avalukkadimaiyAnAy
nindhai seidhavan magan sol kAkka iru uruvAnAy
pandhai ottha aLavu veNNai thirudavendRE nIyum
mandhai mEyppavan pOl vandhAy urugiyE kaNNIr perugi nindRa en
sections.en: You became enamored with a fistful of flattened rice from the poor soul with tattered clothes; you transformed yourself to a half-man, half-lion form to protect the word of the young son of a fellow who constantly insulted you; you appeared as a cowherd just to steal a ball of butter. My mind softened upon hearing all these stories, and my eyes welled with tears.

notes: The charanam of this song describes three tales from Sriman Narayana’s incarnations as Narasimha and Krishna. All three episodes are detailed in the Srimad Bhagavatam. As a young boy, Krishna had a close friend named Sudama, also known as Kuchela. They received their early scriptural education together under the same teacher. During their gurukula days in Sage Sandipani’s ashram, Sudama was devoted to his divine friend. As life progressed, their paths diverged. Sudama continued his Vedic duties as a traditional Brahmin, and many times his wife urged him to visit Krishna. Knowing that Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, was Krishna’s consort, she hoped that if Sudama explained his poverty and difficult circumstances, Krishna might provide the means for them to live comfortably. Kuchela finally agreed to travel to Dwaraka to meet his old friend. He carried a small bundle of flattened rice wrapped in a cloth and slung it over his shoulder. Upon his arrival, Krishna embraced him warmly and reminisced about their school days. Sudama felt hesitant to offer the humble gift of flattened rice, but Krishna joyfully seized the bundle and ate it with delight. Sudama could not bring himself to ask Krishna for a favor. He returned home with only the memory of Krishna’s affection and hospitality. To his astonishment, his modest hut had transformed into a mansion, and his wife was adorned with gold jewelry, attended to by maids. Sudama was deeply moved by Krishna’s compassion and grace. For details, see: ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், இரண்டாம் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, குசேலோபாக்கியானம், பக்கம் 255-268. For more detail about this epic friendship, see Narayaneeyam Dasakam 87. Kuchelopakyanam, Krishna’s grace The demon Hiranyakasipu performed intensive penance while chanting the name of the creator, Lord Brahma. Brahma appeared and granted him a boon that he could not be killed by a human, a beast, or a celestial, and also not be killed during the morning or night. Armed with this boon, the demon became tyrannical, attacking the celestials and proclaiming himself to be God, insisting that no one needed to worship any other deity. Hiranyakasipu had a son named Prahladha, who was born a devoted follower of Lord Vishnu. Prahladha constantly chanted the Lord’s name and spent every moment absorbed in thoughts of Him. Hiranyakasipu became enraged that he could not alter his son’s devotion and tried many times to kill him. One day, in a fit of fury, he drew his sword intending to kill Prahladha. He mockingly asked his son whether his Lord would come to save him. Striking a pillar in anger, he was shocked when Mahavishnu emerged from it in the form of Narasimha—half-lion and half-man. The divine being seized Hiranyakasipu, placed him on His thigh near a doorway at dusk, and tore open his heart with His sharp claws, thus ending the tyrant’s reign on earth. For details, see: ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், முதல் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, பிரஹ்லாத சரித்திரம், பக்கம் 334-377, more specifically பக்கம் 357-361. A well-known story in the Bhagavatham is about the child Krishna stealing butter during his childhood in ஆயர்பாடி (shepherd’s village or town). As a toddler, he was very interested in playful acts such as eating sand, or drinking milk and curd. His mischievous acts, such as breaking pots to eat oozing butter is part of folklore. One such incident during his childhood in Gokulam with his mother Yasoda is described in Bhagavatham 10.9-8. For details see:ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், இரண்டாம் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, கோகுல லீலை பக்கம் 3- 21, more specifically பக்கம் 10 -13. edhugaiyum mOnaiyum எதுகையும் மோனையும் Pallavi எதுகையும் மோனையும் வேண்டுவதோ எம்பெருமான் edhugaiyum mOnaiyum vENduvadhO emperumAn திருவருள் நினைந்து துதிபாடத் துணிந்தார்க்கே thiruvaruL ninaindhu thudhipAdath thuNindhArkkE Anupallavi பாதம் பட்ட இடமெல்லாம் சாபம் நலியும் pAdham patta idamellAm sAbam naliyum திரு உறங்கும் பெரு நகரினிலோ வளம் மலியும் thiru uRangum peru nagarinilO vaLam maliyum Charanam காலணியும் அரசாளும் கார்முகிலும் ஒரு திரண்டு kAlaNiyum arasALum kArmugilum oru thiraNdu பாரெல்லாம் தழைத்திடவே கரைந்து நிற்கும் pArellAm thazhaitthidavE karaindhu niRkum செம்மண் வயலெல்லாம் செழித்து ஓங்கும் semmaN vayalellAm sezhitthu Ongum சீர்மிகு சான்றோரும் மறை முறையே நடந்திடுவார் sIrmigu sAndROrum maRai muRaiyE nadandhiduvAr Translation Pallavi Does anyone who contemplates the grace and compassion of the Lord, and decides to sing His glory, truly need rhymes and alliterations in music? Anupallavi All curses will be annihilated wherever the Lord’s feet touch. Prosperity will overflow in the city where Goddess Lakshmi resides. Charanam Even a mere pair of sandals will rule such a blessed land. Dark clouds will gather and dissolve to bring abundant rainfall, making the earth fertile. The farmlands will yield rich harvests, and the nation will flourish. Noble elders and learned scholars will live guided by the righteous path prescribed in the scriptures, without deviating from orthodoxy. Author’s Note The anupallavi of the song is based on the episode of Ahalya’s sapa vimochanam (release from her curse). This event occurred when Lord Rama’s feet touched the uninhabited hermitage of Sage Gautama. Ahalya, his wife, had once been deceived by Lord Indra and thus incurred Sage Gautama’s wrath. He cursed her to become an inanimate stone, devoid of contact with any living being. Before departing, however, Sage Gautama granted her the boon that she would regain her original form when Lord Rama’s feet touched the hermitage. He also blessed her, saying she could reunite with him after worshipping Lord Rama. For details, see: ஶ்ரீமத் வால்மீகி ராமாயண ஸாரம், உரை ஆசிரியர் அண்ணா, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ணமடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, இரண்டாம் பதிப்பு, அஹல்யா சாப விமோசனம், பக்கம் 82-90. The phrase “kalaniyum arasalum” in the charaṇam refers to an episode from the Ramayana, where Bharata placed Lord Rama’s sandals on the throne and ruled the kingdom as Rama’s representative until His return from exile. It is universally believed that any place where Goddess Lakshmi resides is blessed with boundless prosperity. The author further suggests that the presence of both Rama and Sita together in any place brings an even greater abundance of prosperity.
